metadata.document_title: IIT Delhi Cyber Security & AI Certificate Programme Online

heading: The Complete Curriculum
text:
A Structured Path to AI Security Mastery
Foundations for AI and Cybersecurity
BRIDGE
2 weeks
Topics covered
Python for security automation: integrating NumPy, Pandas, and Jupyter with security data pipelines; API interactions for threat intelligence feeds
ML workflow integration: connecting model training to security evaluation; class imbalance strategies applied to phishing and malware datasets
Security tools setup: Wireshark, Nmap, Burp Suite basics, Kali Linux, Docker, Git workflow
Cloud integration: confirming console access across AWS/Azure/GCP; verifying IAM roles and permissions for subsequent module labs
MITRE ATT&CK introduction: SOC workflow understanding
Cybersecurity Foundations, Threat Modeling, and Threat Landscape
Module 1
3 weeks
Global and India threat landscape: APTs, ransomware, supply chain attacks, UPI fraud, digital arrest scams
MITRE ATT&CK framework deep-dive, cyber kill chain, threat intelligence fundamentals
Threat modeling (STRIDE): assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, mitigation mapping
Identity attacks and defences: OAuth/OIDC flows, JWT misuse, session fixation, refresh token theft, SSO/SAML basics
Vulnerability management, CVSS 4.0, and security operations fundamentals
Skills acquired
AI/ML for Security and Detection Engineering
Module 2
5 weeks
Security data engineering: feature extraction from logs, handling extreme class imbalance
Machine learning for threat detection: malware classification, phishing detection, fraud detection
Security-grade evaluation: calibration, thresholding, cost-of-error analysis, failure modes
MLOps starter: experiment tracking, model registry basics, reproducibility discipline
Detection-as-code fundamentals: Sigma rule syntax, detection logic patterns mapped to ATT&CK
Detection testing: unit tests for rules, coverage analysis, and false positive analysis
SIEM architecture with Elastic Stack: focused log ingestion and correlation
Incident cockpit design: severity scoring, alert correlation, response recommendations
SOAR basics: playbook design principles and human-in-the-loop workflows
Optional self-paced: UEBA behavioural baselines; IR/forensics foundations
Adversarial ML, LLM Security, Agentic AI, and Frontier Attack Surfaces
Module 3
Agentic AI pipeline foundations: LangChain and LangGraph architecture, tool-calling patterns, MCP basics, agent memory, and decision chaining
Adversarial ML fundamentals: evasion, poisoning, and extraction attacks through MITRE ATLAS
OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025): Prompt Injection, Excessive Agency, Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
LLM security and secure RAG: prompt injection (direct and indirect), jailbreaking, data leakage, retrieval poisoning, and data exfiltration via retrieved documents
AI-specific incident response: model rollback, data poisoning forensics, and model integrity verification
LLM red teaming toolstack: PyRIT for automated red teaming, Garak for OWASP LLM Top 10 vulnerability scanning, and PromptBench for prompt robustness evaluation
Multimodal jailbreaks: Multi-Modal Linkage, perceptual transformation exploits, and Visual Scenario Hypnosis in vision-language models
Tool-calling exploitation: function call injection, tool chain exploitation, and parameter poisoning in agentic AI
MCP prompt injection: server-to-server trust override in Model Context Protocol environments
Memory poisoning: trigger-free single-shot poisoning via benign-looking content in long-context LLM agents
Model hub supply chain attacks: namespace hijacking, safetensors conversion exploitation, and detection tooling
MLSecOps, DevSecOps, and India Compliance
Module 4
4 weeks
Implement a DevSecOps + MLSecOps pipeline with policy-as-code enforcement (OPA), runtime detection (Falco), model signing (Sigstore), and AI-BOM generation (Apply)
Produce auditor-ready DPDP Rules 2025 compliance artifacts: breach notification workflow, Consent Manager integration, Data Fiduciary obligations checklist (Create)
Map an organisation's security controls to the SEBI CSCRF 2024 structured audit format, including RE classification tier assignment (Apply)
Document board-level IT risk accountability obligations under RBI Master Directions 2024 with a CERT-In notification playbook (Create)
AI Governance, Global Regulation, Risk Quantification, and Executive Communication
Module 5
AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) with artifact templates; ISO/IEC 42001 AI Management System controls and certification pathway; EU AI Act risk tier taxonomy mapped to NIST AI RMF categories
EU AI Act phased enforcement: Feb 2025 prohibitions active; Aug 2025 GPAI obligations; Aug 2026 high-risk AI (Annexes III/IV); India-facing implications for MNCs
Privacy engineering: privacy-by-design principles (ISO 29101) applied to AI systems; DPDP Rules 2025 mapping to privacy engineering controls
FAIR risk quantification: translating threat scenarios into financial loss distributions using Monte Carlo simulation; presenting output as a board narrative; risk appetite framing
AI ethics in security contexts: bias and fairness in threat detection models; dual-use dilemmas; explainability for forensics and regulatory auditability
Emerging threats and post-quantum readiness: AI-powered attacks, deepfake social engineering, synthetic media fraud detection in BFSI; NIST PQC standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205), hybrid systems, and migration planning
Build & Deploy an AI Security Solution
Capstone
The capstone is the programme's culminating deliverable. Each participant independently designs and builds a complete, production-grade AI security solution - ntegrating all modules - on a real problem they choose.
Projects are evaluated by a panel of IIT Delhi faculty on technical depth, real-world applicability, India regulatory alignment, responsible AI design, and quality of presentation.

heading: What is the Chief Data and AI Officer Program About?
text:
The CDO/CDAIO is the executive who owns the organisation's data and AI strategy - from architecture to monetisation to governance.
Every enterprise today runs on data. But who owns it at the strategic level? Who builds the investment case for data? Who governs AI systems, evaluates vendors, and is personally accountable when they fail? Who ensures compliance across DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI? Who turns analytics from a support function into a driver of innovation and enterprise value? And as AI products scale, who governs the data, risk, and compliance layer they depend on?
That is the CDO/CDAIO mandate.
It is one of the fastest-growing C-suite roles globally - 90% of large enterprises now have one. In India, the role is accelerating, driven by regulatory pressure, AI adoption at scale, and the growing recognition that data leadership requires its own seat at the table.
This program is built for the leader who will hold that mandate.

heading: Prof. C. Ramanathan
text: Professor Chandrashekar Ramanathan is a faculty member at IIIT-B (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore) since 2007 serving as professor, researcher and administrator. He has been working in the field of Computing for over 25 years in various capacities across industry and academia. He has been associated with IIITB for over 15 years where he has been teaching and carrying out research in diverse areas. His expertise lies in the fields of data science, software engineering, and large scale application development. He holds a Ph.D. degree from Mississippi State University, with his research focused on object-oriented databases. His teaching interests are in the areas of data modeling, data analytics, database design, and software architecture. His current research focus is Data Science, Model-based Software Engineering, and Technology for Education. He has authored several research papers and supervised thesis work of four PhD students, who have now graduated from IIIT-B under his guidance. He is currently heading Machine Intelligence and Robotics Center (MINRO) and Center for Technology Research and Innovation – Digital Governance (CTRI-DG), both of which are funded by Government of Karnataka. He is passionate about the use of technology for improving the quality of education. He serves on the Technical Advisory Panels of many departments of the Government of Karnataka including the Department of Education, Finance, and Center for Smart Governance. He also serves as a subject-matter expert on the Board of Studies of several HEI (Higher Educational Institutions). Dr. Chandrashekar was a Board member in the “Board for IT Education Standards (BITES)” between 2013 and 2023. He was recognized in the list of “Top 10 Data Science academicians of India” by the Analytics India magazine for the year 2018 and again in 2019.

metadata.document_title: IIIT-B & IIMU Chief Data and AI Officer Programme Online

heading: Prof. V. Sridhar
text: Dr. V. Sridhar (vsridhar@iiitb.ac.in) is a Professor at the Centre for IT and Public Policy at the International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore, India. He is the author of three books: Telecom Revolution in India: Technology, Regulation and Policy (2012), The Dynamics of Spectrum Management: Legacy, Technology, and Economics (2014), and Emerging ICT Policies and Regulations: Roadmap to Digital Economies (2019). His edited a book titled Data-Centric Living: Algorithms, Digitization and Regulation was published by Routledge (2022). His co-authored new book titled "5G and Beyond: Rewiring Telecom Regulation", has just been published by the Oxford University Press. Dr. Sridhar has taught at many institutions in the USA, Finland, New Zealand and India. He was a Visiting Scholar at the Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism, University of Southern California, U.S.A. during May-June, 2021; April-May, 2022, June 2024 and Mar-July, 2025. He has received funding from different sources, both national and international for his research projects, recent ones being from Facebook. He has been a member of Government of India committees on Telecom and IT and has published many peer-reviewed articles in telecom and information systems journals. He has also written more than 300 article in newspapers and magazines on telecom regulation in India. Dr. Sridhar has a Ph.D. from the University of Iowa, U.S.A. His complete work can be accessed at: http://www.vsridhar.info

heading: Why a Chief Data and AI Officer Program Matters in 2026?
text:
As enterprises scale their data estates and AI adoption accelerates, the Chief Data and AI Officer role has moved from emerging to essential. 90% of large enterprises globally now have a CDO. In India, the role is gaining momentum - driven by DPDP compliance deadlines, AI governance requirements, and the growing need to treat data as a strategic asset rather than a technology input.
Today's CDOs are not just analytics leaders - they own the enterprise data strategy, govern AI systems, build the investment case for data, and are personally accountable for regulatory compliance across DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI. The role demands a combination of technical authority over data architecture and AI, and business authority over data economics, monetisation, and C-suite leadership.
Whether you are a Director of Data looking to step into the CDO role, a Head of AI/ML looking to broaden your mandate, or a Senior Manager in analytics preparing for the next level - this program gives you the frameworks, credentials, and peer network to get there.

heading: The Complete Curriculum
text:
Journey to becoming an AI Product Leader
AI Product Opportunity Discovery
Module 1
Topics covered
AI product landscape - categories, business models, AI-native vs. AI-enhanced
AI Suitability Matrix - probabilistic, learnable, recoverable, data-rich dimensions
TASQ Checklist - Task ambiguity, Scale, Quality tolerance as first-pass filter
AI Opportunity Canvas - data richness, failure recoverability, feedback loop potential
Feasibility assessment - data availability, model capability, cost viability, regulatory risk
Build vs. buy vs. prompt decision framework
AI-Native Product Design
Module 2
Behaviour specifications - constraints, failure modes, fallback paths, confidence thresholds
AI PRD - eval criteria, hallucination risk tiers, data requirements, guardrail specifications
Trust architecture - transparency, confidence calibration, user control
Copilot-Autopilot spectrum as product design decisions
AI UX/UI - chat, inline suggestions, ambient intelligence, co-creation canvas
AI products vs. services vs. platforms - platform readiness decision
AI & GenAI Fluency
Module 3
LLM architecture intuition - transformers, embeddings, tokenisation for product decisions
Foundation model landscape - GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, Sarvam AI, Llama
Token economics in INR - cost-per-query at 1K, 10K, 100K users
Prompt engineering as product design - system prompts, few-shot, chain-of-thought
Build vs. buy vs. prompt vs. fine-tune decision framework
Multimodal AI - vision, voice, and document models in product context
AI Prototyping & Rapid Validation
Module 4
Prompt-to-app prototyping - Bolt.new, Lovable, v0 with live LLM API integration
Multi-turn conversation design and structured output handling
Structured peer review using the AI product review rubric
Prototype audit - documenting 10+ production gaps
Production handoff specification - architecture, security, engineering effort
Prototype-to-production gap analysis and stakeholder presentation
AI Systems & Agentic Design
Module 5
RAG architecture - chunking strategy, vector databases, retrieval failure modes
Agentic workflows - tool use, planning, multi-agent orchestration
MCP (Model Context Protocol) as an integration standard
HITL / HOTL / HOOTL autonomy taxonomy - designing agent boundaries
India Stack as agent infrastructure - UPI, Aadhaar, Account Aggregator
Data flywheel design and infrastructure literacy for PMs
AI Evaluation & Red Teaming
Module 6
Test dataset construction - Gold, Operational, Adversarial, Safety datasets
RAGAS metrics and LLM-as-judge methodology
Quality gates - launch, target, and aspirational thresholds
Adversarial red teaming - prompt injection, jailbreaks, Hinglish adversarial inputs
Hallucination classification - factual, contextual, logical risk tiers
Ship / No-Ship decision protocol based on evaluation evidence
AI Analytics & Experimentation
Module 7
4-Tier AI Metrics Model - model, system, product, and business metrics
AI-native metrics - acceptance rate, override rate, cost-per-correct-output
A/B testing for non-deterministic outputs - shadow deployment, interleaving
Model drift detection - performance monitoring and retraining triggers
Feedback loop design as product operations
Instrumentation spec and experiment design for AI products
AI Product Economics & Go-to-Market
Module 8
LLM unit economics - token + infrastructure + orchestration costs in INR
The whale user problem and cost governance strategy
AI pricing playbook - consumption-based, outcome-based, seat-based models
GTM for AI trust challenges - trust-first positioning and enterprise AI sales
India market channels - WhatsApp, ONDC, GeM, IndiaAI Mission
Change management and stakeholder alignment for AI products
AI Operations, Safety & Compliance
Module 9
DPDP Act 2023 - consent architecture, data minimisation, purpose limitation
NIST AI RMF - risk tiering, documentation, governance framework
EU AI Act risk tiers and prohibited use cases
RBI FREE-AI framework for financial AI products
Production monitoring, model drift response, go/no-go escalation
AI incident response protocol and regulatory notification
Capstone - IIT Faculty Defence
The Proof
AI Opportunity Brief - problem, suitability, feasibility, competitive landscape
AI Product Specification Pack - behaviour spec, AI PRD, trust architecture
Model Selection Brief - 3+ candidates evaluated with INR cost projections
Working AI Prototype + Production Handoff Specification
AI System Architecture + Evaluation Framework + Red Teaming Evidence
AI Product Business Case + GTM Plan
Live model drift crisis injection - go/no-go decision before faculty panel

heading: IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering
text:
The Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur is an 8-month, live online program for working software engineers who need to build AI into the core of their systems, not as a bolted-on feature.
The rush to integrate Generative AI has exposed a critical skills gap in the tech industry. According to Gartner, at least 30% of GenAI projects were abandoned after the proof-of-concept phase by 2025 due to escalating costs, poor risk controls, and a lack of clear business value. While many developers can build a basic RAG demo or call an LLM API, the industry is actively seeking engineers who can deploy scalable, secure, and cost-effective AI systems in live production environments.
The IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering is delivered with upGrad handling admissions and delivery, while the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Kharagpur owns the academic design and certification. It includes:
96 hours of live, faculty-led instruction
An optional foundations bridge for Python or TypeScript gaps
Five core modules plus a capstone project
One integrated system built and deployed end to end

heading: Why Choose the Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur?
text:
India's technology sector is experiencing a significant shortage of AI talent. According to NASSCOM, India now requires more than 1.25 million AI professionals, while industry demand continues to outpace the available talent pool. As AI adoption accelerates across enterprises, organizations are looking beyond prompt engineering and hiring professionals who can build, deploy, and scale production-ready AI systems that deliver measurable business value.
The Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur is built precisely around the wall most engineers hit sooner or later: taking an AI feature from a fragile demo to a robust production system.
Build Production-Ready AI Systems: Every layer connects to the one before it. Frontend calls backend, backend queries retrieval; agents act on all of it, hardened by the production module.
Develop Practical AI Engineering Skills: Every module follows build manually, use AI to accelerate, then audit what AI produced for bugs and security gaps.
Master End-to-End RAG Development: Build a RAG pipeline from raw SDKs, then with a framework, then evaluate both with RAGAS and CI gates.
Solve Real-World Indian Business Use Cases: OCR for PAN, GST, and Aadhaar, multilingual retrieval through Bhashini, INR cost modeling, and WhatsApp Business API and UPI integrations.
Engineer Secure and Compliant AI Applications: DPDP Act 2023 compliance, prompt injection defense, and adversarial red-teaming as engineering deliverables, not an afterthought.

The IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering is built for people already shipping software, not for a first step into tech.
Software Engineers (2+ years): Full-stack, backend, or frontend engineers who ship production software but haven't built AI features into their own products.
ML and AI Engineers (2+ years): Engineers who build models and want to turn experiments into deployed features with cost control and safety.
Tech Leads and Architects: People who need to design the AI layer themselves instead of delegating it to a junior engineer.
This program is generally not for developers with under 2 years of experience, ML researchers focused on training pipelines, Java or C# or Go-only developers with no Python or JS, non-technical professionals, or anyone looking for a quick certificate without hands-on work.

heading: 1 . What is Tableau, and how is it useful for beginners in data visualization?
text: Tableau is a powerful yet user-friendly data visualization tool designed to help users especially beginners, turn raw data into clear, interactive dashboards and visual reports. With Tableau Public (free) or Tableau Desktop (paid), you can connect to spreadsheets, cloud databases, or even web data, and build meaningful visuals without writing a single line of code.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 2 . How do I start using Tableau Desktop for data analysis?
text: If you are new to Tableau, we recommend starting with the free Tableau Desktop Personal Edition. It will allow you to connect to your data, create visualizations, and share them with others. Once you have mastered the basics of Tableau, you can upgrade to the Professional Edition or purchase Tableau Server licenses.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 3 . What is the architecture of Tableau Desktop, and why does it matter?
text: The Tableau Desktop architecture is built around three core layers: Data Layer, Data Engine, and Visualization Layer. This means you can connect to almost any data source, process it quickly using Tableau’s in-memory engine, and then visualize it using a dynamic front-end interface. This architecture allows real-time interaction with large datasets making Tableau software ideal for analysts, marketers, and business teams.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 4 . How is Tableau different from other BI tools?
text: Other BI tools require users to write SQL queries or learn a proprietary scripting language to extract data for analysis. Tableau requires no such queries or scripts - users can simply point and click to analyze data stored in almost any format. In addition, Tableau’s visualizations are highly interactive and allow users to drill down into the data to uncover trends and patterns that would be difficult to spot in raw data.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 5 . What topics are covered in upGrad’s free Tableau certification course?

heading: 1 . What is the history of Natural Language Processing?
text: NLP has a long and rich history, dating back to the early days of computing. In 1950, Alan Turing published his famous paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence", in which he proposed the now-famous Turing test as a way to determine whether a machine could be said to be truly intelligent. This paper is often cited as the beginning of artificial intelligence and NLP research.

Knowledge representation

heading: 19 . Why is the entire amount blocked on my credit card?
text: Initially your bank will block the entire amount from your available purchase limit and from your next billing cycle, you will be charged the EMI amount. As you start paying your EMI, your credit limit will be released accordingly. For example, if you have made a payment of ₹100000 on 6-months EMI and your credit limit is ₹200,000 then initially your bank will block your credit limit by ₹100000. After payment of your first month EMI of Rs.15000, the blocked amount will come down to ₹85000.

heading: 20 . Why is interest getting charged on No Cost EMI?
text: Your bank will charge you interest. However, this interest charge has been provided as an upfront discount at your payment, effectively giving you the benefit of a No-cost EMI. The total amount paid to the bank during the entire EMI tenure will equal the amount paid to upGrad. E.g. Amount payable to upGrad: INR 4,05,000 Let's say the amount deducted during the transaction is INR 3,79,850 (Principal amount). The Bank charges interest of 12-15% per annum on INR 3,79,850 [Note: Interest factor is reducing rate and not Flat rate] EMI AMOUNT = INR 33,750 x 12 = INR 4,05,000 Effectively, you have taken a loan of INR 3,79,850 instead of INR 4,05,000

heading: What are the Skills you’ll acquire in the Doctorate of Business Administration (DBA) from Edgewood University
text:
The Doctorate of Business Administration (DBA) from Edgewood University is designed to empower professionals with advanced skills to lead in complex business environments. This online DBA program combines academic rigor with practical insights, preparing learners to tackle real-world challenges and drive organizational success.
Key Skills Learners Will Gain:
1. Strategic Leadership
Crafting and implementing effective business strategies.
Navigating organizational dynamics and driving growth.
2. Advanced Research and Analysis
Conducting applied business research to solve complex problems.
Leveraging data-driven insights for strategic decision-making.
3. Change Management
Lead organizations through transformation and innovation using frameworks taught in the DBA from Edgewood University.
Building resilience in evolving markets.
4. Global Business Perspective
Understanding international business operations and cultural diversity.
Developing strategies for success in global markets.
5. Financial Expertise
Analyzing financial data for sound decision-making.
Driving business performance through effective financial planning.
6. Ethical and Responsible Leadership
Incorporating ethical principles into business practices.
Leading with integrity in diverse and inclusive environments.
7. Teaching and Consulting Skills
Prepare learners for academic or advisory roles with a strong theoretical and practical foundation.
Guiding others with research-based solutions, a core outcome of the Doctor of Business Administration curriculum.

heading: DBUS 933
text:
BUS 901 - Academic Scholarship and Doctoral Studies
Use critical thinking models and practices, including the role of assumptions, to identify business problems
Topics :
Introduction to Business Research
Identification of the Research Problem
Determination of the Research Design
Identification of the Sampling and Data Collection Strategy
Determination of the Data Analysis Strategy
Presenting Results
BUS 903 - Analyzing Behavior in Organizations
Understand the processes used to analyze organizational behavior, development and leadership
Topics:
Making Sense of Organizations
The Structural Frame
The Human Resource Frame
The Political Frame
The Symbolic Frame
Leadership Practice
BUS 920 - Quantitative Analysis I: Quantitative Research and Analysis
Understand the application of quantitative analytical techniques to problems in business enterprises
Working with Data
Linear Regression
Multiple Regression
Regression Interpretation
Linear Regression Assumptions
BUS 921 - Qualitative Research
Formulate appropriate qualitative research plans, questions, conduct a planned analysis, and communicate their findings
Narrative Methodology
Phenomenological Methodology
Grounded Theory Methodology
Ethnographic Methodology
Case Study Methodology
Qualitative Data Collection and Analysis
BUS 922 - Quantitative Analysis II: Applied Regression Analysis
Execute a quantitative estimation plan that is coherent to both the posed research question(s) and the nature of the necessary/relevant data
Review and Adjustments to OLS
Non-OLS Estimation
Limited Dependent Variable Models
Panel Data
Time Series Data
Event Studies
BUS 902 - Business Ethics & Sustainability
Explore new and emerging sustainable business strategies that create a competitive advantage to support organizations.
Introduction to Ethics, Dominican Values, and Four Theories
Consequentialism and Partnership
Deontology
Virtue Ethics
Social Contract Theory
Sustainability Strategies and Ethics
BUS 910 - Financial Decision-Making and Value Creation
Understand the genesis of the major finance sub-fields and how they have evolved through the fields’ ongoing knowledge creation.
Asset Pricing
Market Efficiency
Frictions and Incentives
Corporate Finance
Derivative Securities
Behavioral Finance
Market Microstructure
BUS 904 - Executive supply chain strategy and negotiations
Identify, dissect, and answer strategic management problems
Inventory, Cost, and Forecasting
Demand Forecasting
Probability-Based Control and Multiechelon Systems
Supply Chain: Finance, Market, and Winning Orders
Supply Chain: The Supply Side Perspective
Negotiations: Culture and Engagement
Negotiations: Perspective and Agreement
DBUS 930 | Applied Doctoral Research Proposal - I
8 Weeks
Students apply the fundamentals of research writing, and how the principles of business research writing will be followed in the applied doctoral research deliverable.
DBUS 931 | Applied Doctoral Research Proposal - I
This part of the proposal contains a synthesis of sufficient academic and business literature to support the need to address the proposed business problem/question.
DBUS 932 | Applied Doctoral Research: Findings and Conclusions
In this deliverable, the students will need to report the findings based on the analysis of collected data.
DBUS 933 | Applied Doctoral Research Defense and Completion
Based on the conclusions about the findings of the study, the students will be expected to recommend the solutions that can be used to address the problem/question. The student will also be expected to prepare an execution plan.

heading: Agentic AI and Generative AI Course Overview
text:
Work practices are changing at a fast pace across engineering, product, and business teams across the globe. AI systems have advanced beyond just answering queries; they are now able to plan work, coordinate workflows, interact with tools and produce tangible results with little human intervention. This emerging field is called Agentic AI.
upGrad offers online courses on Agentic AI and Generative AI for those who want to be prepared for this revolution. Be it a software engineer who wants to create AI native products, a data professional trying to specialize in Large Language Model (LLM), or a business leader who wants to understand and implement intelligent automation, such programs provide skills relevant to the actual professional world.

metadata.document_title: Agentic AI Courses Online, Training & Certification

heading: What Is Generative AI?
text: Generative AI is the type of Artificial Intelligence that has the capability to generate new content based on the information it was trained on. It can comprehend the user query and produce output accordingly and hence is used for performing work related to content creation, coding, research, design, and similar areas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are often used in Generative AI systems.

metadata.document_title: Agentic AI Courses Online, Training & Certification

heading: How Does Generative AI Work?
text:
The generative AI uses trained models for identifying patterns within existing data and generating new data based on user instructions or inputs. The process of working with a generative AI typically involves:
Data: Models learn patterns from large amounts of training data.
Training: AI models are trained to understand language, images, code, audio, or other types of data.
Prompt: You provide an instruction or input to the model.
Processing: The model understands the input and identifies relevant patterns.
Generation: The model creates new content based on the given prompt.

metadata.document_title: Agentic AI Courses Online, Training & Certification

heading: What Is Agentic AI?
text: Agentic AI means AI systems capable of achieving the goal using task planning, reasoning, tool use, API calls, context, and action. Unlike the system that can only provide output for the user's input, an AI agent breaks down the task into smaller pieces and works in a particular workflow with minimum human intervention.

metadata.document_title: Agentic AI Courses Online, Training & Certification

heading: How Do AI Agents Work?
text:
An AI agent combines an AI model with instructions, tools, memory, data, and actions to complete a task. A typical AI agent workflow includes:
Goal: Understand what needs to be completed.
Planning: Break the goal into smaller tasks.
Reasoning: Decide what steps are required.
Tool Use: Access APIs, databases, search systems, or other tools.
Memory: Maintain relevant information and context.
Action: Execute the required tasks.
Evaluation: Check the result and take further action when needed.

metadata.document_title: Agentic AI Courses Online, Training & Certification

heading: What Is the Difference Between Generative AI and Agentic AI?
text:
Generative AI and Agentic AI are related but focus on different capabilities. The key difference between both technologies are:

Text generation, code generation, images, reports, marketing content
Agentic AI
Plans and performs multi-step tasks using models, tools, APIs, and workflows
AI assistants, workflow automation, multi-agent systems, tool-based tasks

heading: Dr. V. Sridhar
text: Dr. V. Sridhar (vsridhar@iiitb.ac.in) is a Professor at the Centre for IT and Public Policy at the International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore, India. He is the author of three books: Telecom Revolution in India: Technology, Regulation and Policy (2012), The Dynamics of Spectrum Management: Legacy, Technology, and Economics (2014), and Emerging ICT Policies and Regulations: Roadmap to Digital Economies (2019). His edited a book titled Data-Centric Living: Algorithms, Digitization and Regulation was published by Routledge (2022). His co-authored new book titled "5G and Beyond: Rewiring Telecom Regulation", has just been published by the Oxford University Press. Dr. Sridhar has taught at many institutions in the USA, Finland, New Zealand and India. He was a Visiting Scholar at the Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism, University of Southern California, U.S.A. during May-June, 2021; April-May, 2022, June 2024 and Mar-July, 2025. He has received funding from different sources, both national and international for his research projects, recent ones being from Facebook. He has been a member of Government of India committees on Telecom and IT and has published many peer-reviewed articles in telecom and information systems journals. He has also written more than 300 article in newspapers and magazines on telecom regulation in India. Dr. Sridhar has a Ph.D. from the University of Iowa, U.S.A. His complete work can be accessed at: http://www.vsridhar.info

heading: Dr. C. Ramanathan
text: Professor Chandrashekar Ramanathan is a faculty member at IIIT-B (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore) since 2007 serving as professor, researcher and administrator. He has been working in the field of Computing for over 25 years in various capacities across industry and academia. He has been associated with IIITB for over 15 years where he has been teaching and carrying out research in diverse areas. His expertise lies in the fields of data science, software engineering, and large scale application development. He holds a Ph.D. degree from Mississippi State University, with his research focused on object-oriented databases. His teaching interests are in the areas of data modeling, data analytics, database design, and software architecture. His current research focus is Data Science, Model-based Software Engineering, and Technology for Education. He has authored several research papers and supervised thesis work of four PhD students, who have now graduated from IIIT-B under his guidance. He is currently heading Machine Intelligence and Robotics Center (MINRO) and Center for Technology Research and Innovation – Digital Governance (CTRI-DG), both of which are funded by Government of Karnataka. He is passionate about the use of technology for improving the quality of education. He serves on the Technical Advisory Panels of many departments of the Government of Karnataka including the Department of Education, Finance, and Center for Smart Governance. He also serves as a subject-matter expert on the Board of Studies of several HEI (Higher Educational Institutions). Dr. Chandrashekar was a Board member in the “Board for IT Education Standards (BITES)” between 2013 and 2023. He was recognized in the list of “Top 10 Data Science academicians of India” by the Analytics India magazine for the year 2018 and again in 2019.

heading: Executive Post Graduate Programme in Forward Deployed AI Engineering
text:
AI deployment is moving beyond the basic model building. Companies and businesses need engineers who can understand a business problem, design the right solution, build AI systems, integrate them into enterprise environments, and take them into production.
The Executive Post Graduate Programme in Forward Deployed AI Engineering from IIIT Bangalore is built for engineers who want to own AI results end-to-end, not just build models in isolation.
The program is delivered by IIIT-B, a NIRF Top 100, NAAC A+ rated institution with alumni network working at Amazon, HSBC, ICICI, Kotak, Microsoft, Jio, and Swiggy. Below is a full breakdown of what it teaches, who it's for, what it costs, and how to apply.

metadata.document_title: Forward Deployed AI Engineering Executive PG Certificate IIIT Bangalore

heading: What is the Executive Post Graduate Programme in Forward Deployed AI Engineering?
text:
This is a 120+ hour, 6-month executive programme designed to train engineers for the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) role: the person who sits at the intersection of client discovery, AI architecture, and production deployment.
Rather than treating GenAI as a standalone skill, the Executive Post Graduate Programme in Forward Deployed AI Engineering teaches learners to scope a client's real problem, build the AI solution, deploy it into the industry environments, and defend the outcome to business stakeholders.
The program includes:
5 hands-on projects across the curriculum
1 live client capstone on Demo Day
A 1-day campus immersion at IIIT Bangalore
Sessions delivered by practicing Forward Deployed Engineers and AI experts, not only academic faculty
IIIT Bangalore alumni status on completion
Anyone searching for a Forward Deployed AI Engineer Course Online will notice most options are either pure GenAI courses or pure cloud-deployment courses. This program combines both GenAI and cloud deployment, making it ideal for professionals who need an Forward Deployed Engineer course online option rather than a full-time, on-campus course.

metadata.document_title: Forward Deployed AI Engineering Executive PG Certificate IIIT Bangalore

heading: Who is a Forward Deployed Engineer?
text:
A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is an engineer who works closely with clients to understand their problems and build solutions that can be used in real-world settings. Instead of stopping after creating a demo, an FDE takes the project from problem identification and solution planning to development and production.
The curriculum of this program reflects this directly, teaching learners to "think like an FDE": client discovery, architecture and solution scoping, not just model training.

88% of companies now use AI in at least one business function, yet most non-technical professionals are stuck choosing between courses that are too technical to follow or too theoretical to apply. This AI for Business Professionals Certificate Program from IIM Kozhikode is designed to eliminate that choice entirely; no coding required.

90+ hours of self-paced content, live workshops, and applied projects

heading: What Is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
text:
AI (Artificial Intelligence) is a technology for simulating human intelligence with computing machines for carrying out activities like language comprehension, problem solving, pattern recognition, and decision making.
AI makes sense out of the data and creates outcomes based on the information gained. Unlike traditional systems that function within pre-set parameters, AI systems have the capability of improving with learning and dealing with new situations.
Some of the widely used AI models include GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and many more. The common ability of these AI models includes language comprehension, creating text, programming, summarizing, translation, and much more.

metadata.document_title: Artificial Intelligence Course Online | Best AI Courses [2026]

heading: How Does Artificial Intelligence Work?
text:
In order to find patterns and produce results, artificial intelligence uses data, algorithms and machine learning models. Depending on the task, an AI system may process data, text, images, video or other information.
In an AI workflow, the following steps are performed:
Data collection: Gather the information needed for the task.
Data preprocessing: Clean and prepare the data for analysis or model training.
Model building: Using machine learning or deep learning methods to create a model.
Training: Train the model with the data to discover patterns.
Evaluation: Test the model to see how it performs.
Application: Use the trained model for prediction, classification, recommendation, automation or other AI tasks.

heading: 12 . What is the difference between AI, ML and Deep Learning?
text:
AI is the wider term for the creation of machines which can do things that normally require intelligence. Machine learning (ML) is a part of AI which allows systems to learn from data and make predictions or decisions.
Deep learning (DL) is a part of ML which involves using multi-layered neural networks for recognizing complex patterns in big amounts of data. To sum up, AI is the more general term, ML is the methodology, while DL is a particular method of ML.

heading: Dr. C. Ramanathan
text: Professor Chandrashekar Ramanathan is a faculty member at IIIT-B (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore) since 2007 serving as professor, researcher and administrator. He has been working in the field of Computing for over 25 years in various capacities across industry and academia. He has been associated with IIITB for over 15 years where he has been teaching and carrying out research in diverse areas. His expertise lies in the fields of data science, software engineering, and large scale application development. He holds a Ph.D. degree from Mississippi State University, with his research focused on object-oriented databases. His teaching interests are in the areas of data modeling, data analytics, database design, and software architecture. His current research focus is Data Science, Model-based Software Engineering, and Technology for Education. He has authored several research papers and supervised thesis work of four PhD students, who have now graduated from IIIT-B under his guidance. He is currently heading Machine Intelligence and Robotics Center (MINRO) and Center for Technology Research and Innovation – Digital Governance (CTRI-DG), both of which are funded by Government of Karnataka. He is passionate about the use of technology for improving the quality of education. He serves on the Technical Advisory Panels of many departments of the Government of Karnataka including the Department of Education, Finance, and Center for Smart Governance. He also serves as a subject-matter expert on the Board of Studies of several HEI (Higher Educational Institutions). Dr. Chandrashekar was a Board member in the “Board for IT Education Standards (BITES)” between 2013 and 2023. He was recognized in the list of “Top 10 Data Science academicians of India” by the Analytics India magazine for the year 2018 and again in 2019.

heading: 20 . Why is the entire amount blocked on my credit card?
text: Initially your bank will block the entire amount from your available purchase limit and from your next billing cycle, you will be charged the EMI amount. As you start paying your EMI, your credit limit will be released accordingly. For example, if you have made a payment of ₹100000 on 6-months EMI and your credit limit is ₹200,000 then initially your bank will block your credit limit by ₹100000. After payment of your first month EMI of Rs.15000, the blocked amount will come down to ₹85000.

heading: 21 . Why is interest getting charged on No Cost EMI?
text: Your bank will charge you interest. However, this interest charge has been provided to you as an upfront discount at the time of your payment, effectively giving you the benefit of a No cost EMI. The total amount paid during the entire EMI tenure to the bank will be equal to the amount to be paid to upGrad. Eg. Amount payable to upGrad: INR 405000 Let's say Amount deducted at the time of transaction: INR 379850 (Principal amount) Bank charges interest of 12-15% per annum on INR 379850 [Note: Interest factor is reducing rate and not Flat rate] EMI AMOUNT = INR 33750 x 12 = INR 405000 Effectively, you have taken loan on 379,850 instead of 405,000

heading: Dr. C. Ramanathan
text: Professor Chandrashekar Ramanathan is a faculty member at IIIT-B (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore) since 2007 serving as professor, researcher and administrator. He has been working in the field of Computing for over 25 years in various capacities across industry and academia. He has been associated with IIITB for over 15 years where he has been teaching and carrying out research in diverse areas. His expertise lies in the fields of data science, software engineering, and large scale application development. He holds a Ph.D. degree from Mississippi State University, with his research focused on object-oriented databases. His teaching interests are in the areas of data modeling, data analytics, database design, and software architecture. His current research focus is Data Science, Model-based Software Engineering, and Technology for Education. He has authored several research papers and supervised thesis work of four PhD students, who have now graduated from IIIT-B under his guidance. He is currently heading Machine Intelligence and Robotics Center (MINRO) and Center for Technology Research and Innovation – Digital Governance (CTRI-DG), both of which are funded by Government of Karnataka. He is passionate about the use of technology for improving the quality of education. He serves on the Technical Advisory Panels of many departments of the Government of Karnataka including the Department of Education, Finance, and Center for Smart Governance. He also serves as a subject-matter expert on the Board of Studies of several HEI (Higher Educational Institutions). Dr. Chandrashekar was a Board member in the “Board for IT Education Standards (BITES)” between 2013 and 2023. He was recognized in the list of “Top 10 Data Science academicians of India” by the Analytics India magazine for the year 2018 and again in 2019.

heading: 1 . What is a Chief Technology Officer?
text: A Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a senior executive responsible for defining an organization's technology vision, innovation strategy, and digital transformation roadmap. CTOs ensure that technology investments support business growth, improve operational efficiency, and create long-term competitive advantage.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

heading: 2 . What does a CTO do differently from a CIO?
text: While a Chief Information Officer (CIO) focuses on managing internal IT systems and operations, a Chief Technology Officer (CTO) leads technology innovation, product architecture, engineering strategy, and emerging technology adoption to drive business growth and customer value.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

heading: 3 . What makes this Chief Technology Officer & AI Leadership Program different from others?
text: The Chief Technology Officer & AI Leadership Program uniquely combines IIIT Bangalore's technical expertise with IIM Udaipur's leadership and business strategy curriculum. It integrates AI, MLOps, platform engineering, FinOps, executive leadership, and business strategy into one comprehensive executive program.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

text: The program runs for 24 weeks (approximately six months) in a blended learning format. Participants attend live weekend sessions, complete recorded pre-work, and dedicate around 7 hours per week, making it suitable for working professionals.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

heading: 6 . Do I need a technical background to apply?
text: The program is primarily designed for professionals with a technology or engineering background. However, senior business leaders and managers responsible for technology strategy, digital transformation, or innovation initiatives can also apply and benefit from the curriculum.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

heading: 7 . Can I pursue this program while working full-time?
text: Yes. The program is specifically designed for working professionals. Its flexible format combines weekend live classes with recorded learning modules, allowing participants to balance their studies with full-time professional responsibilities.

metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

text: The Strategic CTO Dossier is a board-ready leadership portfolio developed throughout all eight modules of the program. metadata.document_title: Chief Technology Officer Program - ​CTO & AI Course & Certification

metadata.document_title: IIT Delhi Cyber Security & AI Certificate Programme Online

heading: The Complete Curriculum
text:
A Structured Path to AI Security Mastery
Foundations for AI and Cybersecurity
BRIDGE
2 weeks
Topics covered
Python for security automation: integrating NumPy, Pandas, and Jupyter with security data pipelines; API interactions for threat intelligence feeds
ML workflow integration: connecting model training to security evaluation; class imbalance strategies applied to phishing and malware datasets
Security tools setup: Wireshark, Nmap, Burp Suite basics, Kali Linux, Docker, Git workflow
Cloud integration: confirming console access across AWS/Azure/GCP; verifying IAM roles and permissions for subsequent module labs
MITRE ATT&CK introduction: SOC workflow understanding
Cybersecurity Foundations, Threat Modeling, and Threat Landscape
Module 1
3 weeks
Global and India threat landscape: APTs, ransomware, supply chain attacks, UPI fraud, digital arrest scams
MITRE ATT&CK framework deep-dive, cyber kill chain, threat intelligence fundamentals
Threat modeling (STRIDE): assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, mitigation mapping
Identity attacks and defences: OAuth/OIDC flows, JWT misuse, session fixation, refresh token theft, SSO/SAML basics
Vulnerability management, CVSS 4.0, and security operations fundamentals
Skills acquired
AI/ML for Security and Detection Engineering
Module 2
5 weeks
Security data engineering: feature extraction from logs, handling extreme class imbalance
Machine learning for threat detection: malware classification, phishing detection, fraud detection
Security-grade evaluation: calibration, thresholding, cost-of-error analysis, failure modes
MLOps starter: experiment tracking, model registry basics, reproducibility discipline
Detection-as-code fundamentals: Sigma rule syntax, detection logic patterns mapped to ATT&CK
Detection testing: unit tests for rules, coverage analysis, and false positive analysis
SIEM architecture with Elastic Stack: focused log ingestion and correlation
Incident cockpit design: severity scoring, alert correlation, response recommendations
SOAR basics: playbook design principles and human-in-the-loop workflows
Optional self-paced: UEBA behavioural baselines; IR/forensics foundations
Adversarial ML, LLM Security, Agentic AI, and Frontier Attack Surfaces
Module 3
Agentic AI pipeline foundations: LangChain and LangGraph architecture, tool-calling patterns, MCP basics, agent memory, and decision chaining
Adversarial ML fundamentals: evasion, poisoning, and extraction attacks through MITRE ATLAS
OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025): Prompt Injection, Excessive Agency, Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
LLM security and secure RAG: prompt injection (direct and indirect), jailbreaking, data leakage, retrieval poisoning, and data exfiltration via retrieved documents
AI-specific incident response: model rollback, data poisoning forensics, and model integrity verification
LLM red teaming toolstack: PyRIT for automated red teaming, Garak for OWASP LLM Top 10 vulnerability scanning, and PromptBench for prompt robustness evaluation
Multimodal jailbreaks: Multi-Modal Linkage, perceptual transformation exploits, and Visual Scenario Hypnosis in vision-language models
Tool-calling exploitation: function call injection, tool chain exploitation, and parameter poisoning in agentic AI
MCP prompt injection: server-to-server trust override in Model Context Protocol environments
Memory poisoning: trigger-free single-shot poisoning via benign-looking content in long-context LLM agents
Model hub supply chain attacks: namespace hijacking, safetensors conversion exploitation, and detection tooling
MLSecOps, DevSecOps, and India Compliance
Module 4
4 weeks
Implement a DevSecOps + MLSecOps pipeline with policy-as-code enforcement (OPA), runtime detection (Falco), model signing (Sigstore), and AI-BOM generation (Apply)
Produce auditor-ready DPDP Rules 2025 compliance artifacts: breach notification workflow, Consent Manager integration, Data Fiduciary obligations checklist (Create)
Map an organisation's security controls to the SEBI CSCRF 2024 structured audit format, including RE classification tier assignment (Apply)
Document board-level IT risk accountability obligations under RBI Master Directions 2024 with a CERT-In notification playbook (Create)
AI Governance, Global Regulation, Risk Quantification, and Executive Communication
Module 5
AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) with artifact templates; ISO/IEC 42001 AI Management System controls and certification pathway; EU AI Act risk tier taxonomy mapped to NIST AI RMF categories
EU AI Act phased enforcement: Feb 2025 prohibitions active; Aug 2025 GPAI obligations; Aug 2026 high-risk AI (Annexes III/IV); India-facing implications for MNCs
Privacy engineering: privacy-by-design principles (ISO 29101) applied to AI systems; DPDP Rules 2025 mapping to privacy engineering controls
FAIR risk quantification: translating threat scenarios into financial loss distributions using Monte Carlo simulation; presenting output as a board narrative; risk appetite framing
AI ethics in security contexts: bias and fairness in threat detection models; dual-use dilemmas; explainability for forensics and regulatory auditability
Emerging threats and post-quantum readiness: AI-powered attacks, deepfake social engineering, synthetic media fraud detection in BFSI; NIST PQC standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205), hybrid systems, and migration planning
Build & Deploy an AI Security Solution
Capstone
The capstone is the programme's culminating deliverable. Each participant independently designs and builds a complete, production-grade AI security solution - ntegrating all modules - on a real problem they choose.
Projects are evaluated by a panel of IIT Delhi faculty on technical depth, real-world applicability, India regulatory alignment, responsible AI design, and quality of presentation.

heading: What is the Chief Data and AI Officer Program About?
text:
The CDO/CDAIO is the executive who owns the organisation's data and AI strategy - from architecture to monetisation to governance.
Every enterprise today runs on data. But who owns it at the strategic level? Who builds the investment case for data? Who governs AI systems, evaluates vendors, and is personally accountable when they fail? Who ensures compliance across DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI? Who turns analytics from a support function into a driver of innovation and enterprise value? And as AI products scale, who governs the data, risk, and compliance layer they depend on?
That is the CDO/CDAIO mandate.
It is one of the fastest-growing C-suite roles globally - 90% of large enterprises now have one. In India, the role is accelerating, driven by regulatory pressure, AI adoption at scale, and the growing recognition that data leadership requires its own seat at the table.
This program is built for the leader who will hold that mandate.

heading: Prof. C. Ramanathan
text: Professor Chandrashekar Ramanathan is a faculty member at IIIT-B (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore) since 2007 serving as professor, researcher and administrator. He has been working in the field of Computing for over 25 years in various capacities across industry and academia. He has been associated with IIITB for over 15 years where he has been teaching and carrying out research in diverse areas. His expertise lies in the fields of data science, software engineering, and large scale application development. He holds a Ph.D. degree from Mississippi State University, with his research focused on object-oriented databases. His teaching interests are in the areas of data modeling, data analytics, database design, and software architecture. His current research focus is Data Science, Model-based Software Engineering, and Technology for Education. He has authored several research papers and supervised thesis work of four PhD students, who have now graduated from IIIT-B under his guidance. He is currently heading Machine Intelligence and Robotics Center (MINRO) and Center for Technology Research and Innovation – Digital Governance (CTRI-DG), both of which are funded by Government of Karnataka. He is passionate about the use of technology for improving the quality of education. He serves on the Technical Advisory Panels of many departments of the Government of Karnataka including the Department of Education, Finance, and Center for Smart Governance. He also serves as a subject-matter expert on the Board of Studies of several HEI (Higher Educational Institutions). Dr. Chandrashekar was a Board member in the “Board for IT Education Standards (BITES)” between 2013 and 2023. He was recognized in the list of “Top 10 Data Science academicians of India” by the Analytics India magazine for the year 2018 and again in 2019.

heading: Why a Chief Data and AI Officer Program Matters in 2026?
text:
As enterprises scale their data estates and AI adoption accelerates, the Chief Data and AI Officer role has moved from emerging to essential. 90% of large enterprises globally now have a CDO. In India, the role is gaining momentum - driven by DPDP compliance deadlines, AI governance requirements, and the growing need to treat data as a strategic asset rather than a technology input.
Today's CDOs are not just analytics leaders - they own the enterprise data strategy, govern AI systems, build the investment case for data, and are personally accountable for regulatory compliance across DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI. The role demands a combination of technical authority over data architecture and AI, and business authority over data economics, monetisation, and C-suite leadership.
Whether you are a Director of Data looking to step into the CDO role, a Head of AI/ML looking to broaden your mandate, or a Senior Manager in analytics preparing for the next level - this program gives you the frameworks, credentials, and peer network to get there.

metadata.document_title: IIIT-B & IIMU Chief Data and AI Officer Programme Online

heading: Who Can Pursue This Chief Data and AI Officer Program?
text:
This program brings together data and AI depth with business strategy and CDO-level leadership - so you don't need to be purely a data engineer or purely a business leader. What you need is experience in data and analytics, ambition for the CDO role, and readiness for organisation-wide impact.
It is ideal for:
Data and analytics leaders currently holding roles like Director Data Analytics, VP Analytics, Head of Data Engineering, Head of AI/ML, Head of Data Products, or Head of BI - in organisations across BFSI, GCCs, IT/ITES, and healthcare.
Professionals with 8+ years of experience in data, analytics, AI/ML, or data engineering, aiming to step into the CDO/CDAIO role.
Strategic thinkers who want to own data and AI strategy, govern AI systems, build data monetisation models, navigate India's regulatory grid, and lead execution at the C-suite level.

text:
The CDO/CDAIO Role is One of the Fastest-Growing C-Suite Mandates in India Regulatory pressure from DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI is forcing organisations to appoint a leader who owns data governance, AI strategy, and compliance. The CDO/CDAIO is that leader - owning the data and AI strategy from architecture to monetisation to execution. Demand is accelerating and the window to establish yourself in this role is now.
The Only Program in India Built Exclusively for the CDO/CDAIO Mandate Not a generalist data or AI program. Not a technology leadership program with a data module. Every module, simulation, and deliverable is designed around the CDO mandate - data architecture, AI governance, data monetisation, regulatory compliance, and C-suite leadership. Built for senior data and analytics leaders targeting the CDO/CDAIO role.
Built for the Indian Data and AI Reality DPDP, RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, India-specific monetisation models, and Indian organisation change dynamics built into the curriculum. 14 case studies drawn from Indian enterprises. This program is designed for the regulatory and commercial environment Indian data and analytics leaders actually operate in.
Drive Innovation Across Industries with a Transferable Mandate Whether you are in BFSI, a GCC, healthcare, telecom, or IT/ITES - data governance, AI strategy, analytics, and regulatory compliance are universal CDO responsibilities. This program gives you frameworks to drive data-driven innovation and long-term strategic growth across sectors.
Execution-Focused Learning 7 CDO Decision Labs. A CDO Strategic Dossier built on your organisation's data. A final defence under surprise constraint before a live panel. Every learning outcome is built around real CDO execution - not hypothetical scenarios.
IIM Udaipur - Business and Strategic Authority for the CDO Mandate Data economics, monetisation strategy, data-first org design, analytics literacy deployment, and C-suite coalition building - delivered by IIM Udaipur, AACSB accredited and ranked among the top 6% of business schools worldwide. Equal depth on the business half and the technical half. That is what the CDO mandate requires.
GenAI and Agentic AI - Own the Governance, Drive the Innovation GenAI and agentic AI are moving from pilots to production across Indian organisations. The CDO/CDAIO owns this transition - evaluating when to deploy, selecting vendors, ensuring data quality for retrieval and inference, auditing agent decisions, and leading incident response. This program builds the AI governance and innovation frameworks to lead that mandate with confidence.

heading: 1 . What is a Chief Data and AI Officer?
text: A Chief Data and AI Officer (CDO/CDAIO) leads an organization's data and AI strategy, including architecture, governance, monetization, compliance, and innovation. The role is also accountable for AI governance and regulatory compliance across DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI.

metadata.document_title: IIIT-B & IIMU Chief Data and AI Officer Programme Online

heading: 2 . How is the CDO/CDAIO different from the CTO?
text: The CTO is responsible for building and operating technology and AI systems, while the CDO/CDAIO owns the data layer, including governance, quality, compliance, and monetization, and oversees AI governance across the organization.

metadata.document_title: IIIT-B & IIMU Chief Data and AI Officer Programme Online

heading: 3 . What industries hire CDOs and CDAIOs?
text: CDOs and CDAIOs are hired across BFSI, GCCs, IT/ITES, healthcare, telecom, e-commerce, manufacturing, AI-first startups, product-led technology firms, and organizations managing data governance and AI strategy at scale.

metadata.document_title: IIIT-B & IIMU Chief Data and AI Officer Programme Online

text: This is the only program in India designed exclusively for analytics and data professionals aiming for the Chief Data and AI Officer (CDO/CDAIO) role. It includes India's regulatory frameworks (DPDP, RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI) into practical operating models and features seven CDO Decision Labs, a CDO Strategic Dossier defended under surprise constraints, and dual alumni status from IIIT Bangalore and IIM Udaipur.

Integrate OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs with streaming, structured outputs, prompt versioning

Instrument per-request cost attribution, user-level spend alerts, async processing
Give Claude Code your Pydantic schemas and service spec. Let it generate the entire FastAPI service. Audit for security gaps, missing resilience patterns, cost-tracking holes. The audit is graded.
Retrieval, Context Engineering & Evaluation
Module 3
Build a complete RAG pipeline from scratch with only SDKs and HTTP calls
Design an abstraction layer resilient to LangChain/LlamaIndex version churn
Implement multi-tenant retrieval with pgvector, row-level security

Evaluate with RAGAS (faithfulness, relevancy, precision, recall) + CI regression gates

Agentic Engineering & Protocol Design
Module 4
Design the perceive-reason-act-observe loop; React and plan-and-execute patterns
Build stateful agents with LangGraph: state machines, tool contracts, checkpointing
Build an MCP server with authentication, least-privilege permissions, audit logging
Design prompt-injection-aware tools; survey emerging A2A and browser-use patterns
Implement human approval gates (>₹1K), escalation workflows, multi-agent coordination
Integrate WhatsApp Business API, UPI, GST validation, DigiLocker
Expose your M2/M3 project as an MCP server. Connect it to Claude. The safety analysis of what could go wrong is the primary assessment.
AI Systems Reliability, Security & Governance

Langfuse: alerting, SLA dashboards, cost anomaly detection
Semantic caching with Redis (40-60% savings)
Intelligent model routing + budget enforcement
CI/CD evaluation gates blocking regressions
Semantic prompt versioning + model-version tracking
Zero-downtime deployment of complete system
OWASP LLM Top 10 + Promptfoo red-teaming (30+ tests)
DPDP Act 2023 as code: consent, erasure, minimisation
Incident response: rollback, post-mortem methodology
Ask Claude to generate a complete DPDP implementation. Audit every artefact against the actual DPDP Rules 2025. Your audit is the assessment.

heading: IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering
text:
The Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur is an 8-month, live online program for working software engineers who need to build AI into the core of their systems, not as a bolted-on feature.
The rush to integrate Generative AI has exposed a critical skills gap in the tech industry. According to Gartner, at least 30% of GenAI projects were abandoned after the proof-of-concept phase by 2025 due to escalating costs, poor risk controls, and a lack of clear business value. While many developers can build a basic RAG demo or call an LLM API, the industry is actively seeking engineers who can deploy scalable, secure, and cost-effective AI systems in live production environments.
The IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering is delivered with upGrad handling admissions and delivery, while the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Kharagpur owns the academic design and certification. It includes:
96 hours of live, faculty-led instruction
An optional foundations bridge for Python or TypeScript gaps
Five core modules plus a capstone project
One integrated system built and deployed end to end

heading: Why Choose the Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur?
text:
India's technology sector is experiencing a significant shortage of AI talent. According to NASSCOM, India now requires more than 1.25 million AI professionals, while industry demand continues to outpace the available talent pool. As AI adoption accelerates across enterprises, organizations are looking beyond prompt engineering and hiring professionals who can build, deploy, and scale production-ready AI systems that deliver measurable business value.
The Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering from IIT Kharagpur is built precisely around the wall most engineers hit sooner or later: taking an AI feature from a fragile demo to a robust production system.
Build Production-Ready AI Systems: Every layer connects to the one before it. Frontend calls backend, backend queries retrieval; agents act on all of it, hardened by the production module.
Develop Practical AI Engineering Skills: Every module follows build manually, use AI to accelerate, then audit what AI produced for bugs and security gaps.
Master End-to-End RAG Development: Build a RAG pipeline from raw SDKs, then with a framework, then evaluate both with RAGAS and CI gates.
Solve Real-World Indian Business Use Cases: OCR for PAN, GST, and Aadhaar, multilingual retrieval through Bhashini, INR cost modeling, and WhatsApp Business API and UPI integrations.
Engineer Secure and Compliant AI Applications: DPDP Act 2023 compliance, prompt injection defense, and adversarial red-teaming as engineering deliverables, not an afterthought.

metadata.document_title: Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering

heading: Who Should Enroll in the Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering?
text:
The IIT Kharagpur Executive Post Graduate Certificate in AI-Native Software Engineering is built for people already shipping software, not for a first step into tech.
Software Engineers (2+ years): Full-stack, backend, or frontend engineers who ship production software but haven't built AI features into their own products.
ML and AI Engineers (2+ years): Engineers who build models and want to turn experiments into deployed features with cost control and safety.
Tech Leads and Architects: People who need to design the AI layer themselves instead of delegating it to a junior engineer.
This program is generally not for developers with under 2 years of experience, ML researchers focused on training pipelines, Java or C# or Go-only developers with no Python or JS, non-technical professionals, or anyone looking for a quick certificate without hands-on work.

heading: 2 . How do I start using Tableau Desktop for data analysis?
text: If you are new to Tableau, we recommend starting with the free Tableau Desktop Personal Edition. It will allow you to connect to your data, create visualizations, and share them with others. Once you have mastered the basics of Tableau, you can upgrade to the Professional Edition or purchase Tableau Server licenses.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 3 . What is the architecture of Tableau Desktop, and why does it matter?
text: The Tableau Desktop architecture is built around three core layers: Data Layer, Data Engine, and Visualization Layer. This means you can connect to almost any data source, process it quickly using Tableau’s in-memory engine, and then visualize it using a dynamic front-end interface. This architecture allows real-time interaction with large datasets making Tableau software ideal for analysts, marketers, and business teams.

metadata.document_title: Tableau Courses Online

heading: 4 . How is Tableau different from other BI tools?
text: Other BI tools require users to write SQL queries or learn a proprietary scripting language to extract data for analysis. Tableau requires no such queries or scripts - users can simply point and click to analyze data stored in almost any format. In addition, Tableau’s visualizations are highly interactive and allow users to drill down into the data to uncover trends and patterns that would be difficult to spot in raw data.

heading: 1 . What is a Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) degree online?
text:
A Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) online is a professional doctoral degree that develops advanced business leadership, strategic decision-making, and applied research expertise. Universities design this program for experienced professionals who want to solve real business problems using evidence-based research.
Unlike traditional full-time doctoral study, online DBA programs offer flexible learning formats. Professionals attend virtual classes, complete research projects, and write a dissertation while continuing their careers.
Many learners in India pursue DBA programs through global academic partnerships offered by upGrad, which enable them to access international faculty, structured research guidance, and industry-focused doctoral training without relocating abroad.

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 2 . Is a DBA a terminal degree?
text:
Yes, a DBA is a terminal degree in business administration. It represents the highest academic qualification in the business field, similar in academic level to a PhD.
Professionals who earn a DBA demonstrate advanced expertise in leadership, strategy, and applied research. This level of education qualifies individuals for senior executive roles, consulting positions, and academic teaching opportunities.
Organizations recognize terminal degrees as proof of deep domain mastery and strategic capability. Many senior professionals pursue a DBA to strengthen credibility, enhance decision-making authority, and gain recognition as subject-matter experts within their industries.

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 3 . What topics do online DBA courses cover?
text:
Online DBA programs cover advanced business topics that combine leadership practice with research-driven problem solving. The curriculum focuses on strategic thinking, organizational performance, and innovation.
Typical topics include:
Strategic management and competitive positioning
Organizational leadership and change management
Business analytics and data-driven decisions
Financial strategy and corporate governance
Research methodology and applied business research
Innovation and digital transformation

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 4 . What is the typical curriculum of an online DBA course?
text:
Most online DBA courses follow a structured pathway that moves from advanced coursework to independent doctoral research.
Typical structure includes:
Phase 1 – Doctoral Coursework
Advanced leadership and business strategy
Research design and methodology
Data analysis techniques
Phase 2 – Research Development
Research proposal development
Literature review
Research framework design
Phase 3 – Dissertation
Original research project
Business problem analysis
Final thesis defense

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 5 . Do online DBA programs require a dissertation?
text:
Yes, most online DBA programs require a dissertation. The dissertation represents the core academic requirement and demonstrates the learner’s ability to conduct original applied research.
Professionals identify a real business challenge, design a research study, collect data, and propose evidence-based solutions. Faculty advisors guide each stage of the research process.
The dissertation typically involves:
Research proposal development
Data collection and analysis
Practical business recommendations
Final academic defense
This research component distinguishes the DBA from shorter executive programs and establishes doctoral-level expertise.

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 6 . Are online DBA programs worth it?
text:
Online DBA programs deliver strong professional and intellectual value for experienced professionals seeking leadership growth. The degree strengthens strategic thinking, research capability, and executive decision-making.
Many professionals pursue a DBA to:
Move into C-suite or senior leadership roles
Transition into consulting or advisory careers
Gain academic teaching opportunities
Develop authority in specialized domains
For many mid-career and senior professionals, a DBA becomes a powerful differentiator in competitive leadership environments. Structured global programs offered through upGrad.com also help learners access international doctoral education with flexible learning and industry-focused research support.

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 7 . Will an online DBA degree help internationally?
text:
An online DBA degree can support international career opportunities when accredited universities offer it and global academic standards guide its curriculum. Employers and institutions worldwide recognize doctoral qualifications that demonstrate advanced research capability, strategic expertise, and leadership competence.
Professionals with a DBA often pursue global consulting roles, international leadership positions, or academic opportunities across countries. Programs delivered through internationally partnered platforms like upGrad.com provide access to globally recognized universities, which strengthens international credibility. The degree’s global acceptance ultimately depends on accreditation, institutional reputation, and research quality.

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 8 . How is a DBA different from a PhD in business administration?
text:
A DBA focuses on applied research and business practice, while a PhD emphasizes theoretical research and academic knowledge creation.
Key differences include:
DBA
Solves real organizational problems
Designed for working professionals
Industry-focused outcomes
PhD
Develops new theoretical models
Prepares primarily for academic research careers
Strong emphasis on scholarly publication

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 9 . DBA vs PhD in Business: which should one choose?
text:
A professional should choose based on career goals. Individuals seeking industry leadership, consulting authority, or executive roles typically benefit more from a DBA.
Individuals who want university research careers or full-time academic scholarship may find a PhD more suitable.
Decision factors include:
Career path preference
Interest in practical vs theoretical research
Work experience level
Desired professional outcomes

metadata.document_title: Doctor of Business Administration - Doctorate Courses & Degree Online

heading: 10 . Online DBA vs in-person DBA: what is the difference?
text:

Online DBA
